security_invariant: Every shell metacharacter in an untrusted argument must be escaped before the quoted value is passed to a command shell.
attacker_controlled_source: String elements supplied to the exported quote function.
missing_or_incorrect_control: The optional Windows drive-letter prefix uses the broad [A-z] character range instead of [A-Za-z].
sensitive_operation: A consumer passes the returned quoted command text to a real shell.
vulnerable_behavior: Characters between Z and a, including the backtick shell metacharacter, can be consumed by the drive-letter branch instead of being escaped.
fixed_behavior: The drive-letter prefix accepts ASCII letters only, so shell metacharacters remain subject to escaping.
root_cause: An over-broad regular-expression character class in the Windows drive-letter special case suppresses escaping for shell metacharacters such as backticks.
required_evidence: Trace an attacker-controlled quote input through index.js.
Show how [A-z] includes non-letter ASCII metacharacters.
Show that the affected character is not escaped in output.
refutation_checks: Check whether the returned value is ever executed by a shell.
Distinguish shell execution from argv-based process spawning.
